- Prompt's Inject, Persona and Group controls serve different purposes. An injection wraps a message; a Persona supplies a reusable identity/instruction configuration; a Group coordinates participants.

# Read a Group's actual conversation order

- Sequential Group response order can be shuffled; later responders can see earlier responses in that round. Read the supplied order instead of assuming alphabetical order.
- Parallel participants respond to the round's existing context; synchronization makes the other replies available for the next message.

**Offline question:** `A box has 3 red and 2 blue tiles. Count all tiles and check the count.` Participants A and B start with this same question.

**Sequential trace, chosen order B then A:** B: `5 tiles: 3 + 2.` A receives B's reply and says `I checked B: 5.`

**Parallel trace:** A: `5 tiles.` B: `3 + 2 = 5.` Neither saw the other's current-round response before generating. Both replies are then synchronized. Next-round question: `Where did you agree?` can refer to both replies.

A Group is not a blinded Compare vote or a fixed pipeline that passes only its previous output. A stopped Group prevents further group progression; do not assume stopping removes already-created conversation content.

**Persistence and availability card:** Group G names owned participant sessions A/B and a parent P. Successful supplied persistence receipts retain the parent question and participant replies in those sessions. A failed persistence request proves no saved copy merely because a reply was visible. Stop aborts current group controllers, clears active participants and removes the local Group-state key; it does not delete the saved sessions. If B’s route is unavailable or a participant is outside the authorized scope, record that missing participation rather than inventing B’s reply.

cases.title: Read a Group's actual conversation order

# Preview owner defaults and pinned decisions

- General Hexes are versioned owner defaults, separate from workspace enforcement. Untagged entries apply owner-wide; tagged entries match any current workspace/task tag, case-insensitively.
- Composition checks owner and sorts by ID/revision. Disabled, unaccepted, unmatched and budget-omitted entries have distinct reasons. Current explicit user instructions take precedence; the General budget does not trim workspace rules.

**Offline owner A, workspace tags [Writing], task tags [review], General budget 50 characters:**

| ID/revision | Title | Body | Tags | Enabled | Accepted |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| a/1 | Short | Be brief. | none | yes | yes |
| b/1 | Review | Check facts. | REVIEW | yes | yes |
| c/1 | Off | Use bullets. | Writing | no | yes |
| d/1 | Draft | Cite sources. | Writing | yes | no |
| e/1 | Code | Test changes. | Coding | yes | yes |

The rendered a block is `General default: Short [revision 1]\nBe brief.` (45 characters). The b block needs 49 characters plus the 2-character separator; it matches but exceeds the remaining 5. Outcomes: a included; b omitted-for-budget; c disabled; d unaccepted; e unmatched. A record owned by B makes this owner-A composition invalid instead of silently importing B's defaults.

**No-context-tags variant:** keep owner A, the same five table entries and the same 50-character budget, but set workspace tags [] and task tags []. Outcomes: a included (45 characters); b unmatched; c disabled; d unaccepted; e unmatched. Untagged a remains owner-wide; b no longer reaches the budget check because no context tag matches.

Boundary T pins the original tagged snapshot. Later enabling c changes a new preview, not T's saved snapshot.

**Promotion card:** workspace rule W says `Preserve a recoverable preimage before editing practice/*.md`. Reviewed draft D preserves W's original source/provenance and proposes General body `Preserve a recoverable preimage before editing.` Saving accepted D creates new General identity G, revision 1; W remains unchanged. Removing tags makes G owner-wide, so review that broader scope explicitly. Tags select contexts, not filesystem path enforcement. Assisted drafts need acceptance. Versioned same-owner import creates a new identity with provenance; it does not secretly replace W.

Before saving a promotion or applying a draft, review its exact current revision/hash and required owner acceptance. Updating a governing workspace rule still needs its own owner authorization; executable checks still need separate trust.

# Save the inbound client's actual scopes

- Settings → Integrations can offer Add Codex Agent or Add Claude Agent for an external client calling Open Clank. Token administration needs the appropriate app authority.
- Follow the direction: client C → Open Clank uses external-client token T; Open Clank → provider uses provider credential P. Neither is the application's browser login session.

**Offline card:** owner A has provider route P and creates client C's token T. The secret is displayed once; the server stores its hash. Newly created T has persisted scopes `[chat]`. The visible preview has all tool toggles selected, but no scope-saving PATCH has succeeded. T still has only chat. Save succeeds with scopes `[chat, documents:read]`; only then is that added scope persisted. For an existing token, a toggle can issue its PATCH immediately; inspect the actual result.

**Access variants:** saved documents:read scope plus an available backend permits reading A's authorized document. A request for another owner's document is denied. An email action is not in the saved scopes. A revoked T authorizes none of these actions.

T and P are symbolic identifiers, not secrets. This exercise needs no token creation, agent installation or live external request.

**Unavailable and revocation cards:** T has saved documents:read but the document backend is unavailable: access cannot complete. Revoke T to end this client’s inbound access; that does not revoke provider credential P or log out the browser application session.
